trait_value_raw: Casuarina equisetifolia occurs naturally along tropical and subtropical sandy coastlines. In Peninsular Malaysia it occurs wild as a light-demanding pioneer tree on sandy coasts, on open sand above the high-water mark where it forms a strip of forest (Corner, 1988). The fallen twigs prevent self regeneration, and often seedlings of Syzygium grande (Wight) Walp. become established in the shade of the Casuarina trees, and eventually transform the vegetation into S. grande forest with a narrow strip of Casuarina on the seaward side.

trait_value_raw: Mabberley (2008) reported that it produces the 'best firewood in the world'. In Peninsular Malaysia, it is commonly planted as an ornamental tree and is also used for hedges and topiary because it is easily pruned. Being a pioneer seashore tree, it is important as a windbreak for coastal resorts.
